chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Zayd al-Bursi, from some of his companions, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to wash his head with sidr (jujube leaves) and say: Wash your heads with the leaves of sidr, for it is sanctified by every near angel and every sent prophet.
And whoever washes his head with the leaves of sidr, Allah will turn away the whisperings of Satan from him for seventy days.
And whoever Allah turns away the whisperings of Satan from for seventy days, he does not disobey.
And whoever does not disobey, will enter Paradise.

key_terms.السِّدْر: Sidr (jujube leaves), a plant used for ritual washing and purification.
key_terms.قَدَّسَهُ: He sanctified it / considered it holy.
key_terms.وَسْوَسَةَ الشَّیْطَانِ: The whisperings or temptations of Satan.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of washing the head with jujube leaves according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.s.) is reported to have used sidr (jujube) leaves for head washing, a practice attributed with spiritual efficacy by both angels and prophets. The hadith establishes a causal chain where this ritual repels Satan's whisperings for seventy days, ensuring a state of obedience that ultimately guarantees entry into Paradise, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the purifying power of specific physical acts when accompanied by divine promise.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) says that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.s.) used to wash his head with Jujube leaves and say, “Wash your head with jujube leaves for all the angels and prophets  consider  this  holy.
Allah  will  keep  away  evil thoughts  of  Shaitaan  for  seventy  days  from  the  one  who washes  his  head  with  jujube  leaves.
and one who does not commit sins will enter Paradise.”
